sop_modules.name: Exterior Window Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Mask glass panes (method driven by Low-E status and muntin type), remove operable window hardware (labeled bags), protect weatherstripping (pull out friction-fit or deep-tape non-removable), protect finished sill (if already painted), protect finished casing (if already painted), mask adjacent siding (spray only), stage brush or spray equipment. Hardware is REMOVED per doctrine — not masked.

tasks.name: Glass Masking — Tape and Film Method
tasks.description: Apply exterior-grade UV-resistant tape (14-day minimum) at glass-to-frame edge, position fine-line tape at 1/16 inch glass lap line, then apply HDPE static-cling masking film over glass pane. Secure secondary tape line to prevent film flutter from wind during exterior work. SAFE for Low-E glass. For single-lite windows: 0.08-0.12 hrs/EA.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Fine-line tape at glass lap line. Film secured against wind.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete glass coverage. Precision fine-line tape placement. Verify seal at all tape edges.
quality_notes.QT5: Complete glass coverage. Premium fine-line tape for razor-sharp glass lap line. Double-check all edges for potential bleed-through.

tasks.notes: Default masking method for Low-E glass (most NC windows). Also used for non-Low-E single-lite, SDL, and GBG windows. HDPE film is static-cling — no adhesive contact with glass.

tasks.name: Glass Masking — Liquid Mask Method (TDL Non-Low-E Only)
tasks.description: Brush-apply liquid masking product (Jasco Mask & Peel) over each individual glass pane in TDL (true divided lite) window. Cure into protective membrane. Dramatically faster than tape-and-film on multi-lite TDL windows. PROHIBITED on Low-E glass — scoring during removal damages Low-E coating permanently.

quality_notes.all: Heavy, even application over each pane. Allow full cure before painting. Score trim line cleanly for peel removal.

tasks.notes: Only valid when Low-E = false AND muntin_type = TDL. For TDL with Low-E glass, fall back to TSK_XWIN_MASK_GLASS_TDL_TAPE.

tasks.name: Glass Masking — Tape and Film for TDL (Low-E or Preference)
tasks.description: Individually mask each glass pane in TDL (true divided lite) window with tape at each muntin bar edge, then film over each pane. Dramatically more time-intensive than liquid mask: 0.20-0.50 hrs/EA depending on lite count. Required for Low-E TDL windows where liquid mask is prohibited.

quality_notes.QT3: Each pane individually masked. Tape sealed at muntin bar edges.
quality_notes.QT4: Each pane individually masked. Fine-line tape at 1/16 inch glass lap on each lite.
quality_notes.QT5: Each pane individually masked. Premium fine-line tape for razor-sharp glass lap on every lite. Double-check all edges.

tasks.notes: TDL with Low-E glass. Highest masking labor of all configurations. Also used as fallback when liquid mask is not preferred on non-Low-E TDL.

tasks.name: Window Hardware Removal
tasks.description: Remove ALL operable window hardware: locks, lifts, sash pulls, crank handles. Place each window's hardware in labeled ziplock bag with window location and contents. Fixed windows have no operable hardware — skip. Areas beneath hardware must be accessible for priming and painting.

quality_notes.all: Full hardware removal. Labeled bags per window. Fixed windows: no hardware to remove.

tasks.notes: Fixed windows excluded — no operable hardware. Bay/bow windows may have multiple hardware sets per assembly.

tasks.name: Weatherstrip Protection
tasks.description: Protect weatherstripping from paint contact. Friction-fit stripping: gently pull out, store safely for re-insert after finish dries. Non-removable stripping: push low-tack tape deep into gap between frame and stripping with putty knife. NEVER paint weatherstripping — destroys elasticity, causes brittleness and seal tearing. Fixed windows have no weatherstripping.

quality_notes.all: Verify stripping is fully protected or removed before any prime/finish work. No paint contact with stripping material.

tasks.name: Exterior Sill Protection
tasks.description: Apply tape and paper/film over finished exterior window sill to catch drips during frame and sash painting. Only needed when sill is already finished (from trim spec). If sill is painted simultaneously with window, no protection needed — coordinate sequence.

quality_notes.all: Complete sill surface coverage. Secure tape edges against wind.

tasks.notes: Conditional on sill being already finished. Cross-spec coordination with SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1.

tasks.name: Adjacent Casing Edge Protection
tasks.description: Apply light tape at casing-to-frame junction when casing is already finished. Prevents drip damage to finished casing during window frame painting. Minimal masking — only at junction line.

quality_notes.all: Light tape at junction. Only when casing is already finished.

tasks.notes: Conditional on casing being already finished. Cross-spec coordination with SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1.

tasks.name: Adjacent Siding Masking (Spray Only)
tasks.description: Mask finished siding adjacent to window to prevent overspray during spray application. Paper and tape over siding surface around window perimeter. Only applicable when application_method = spray. Brush application has minimal overspray — no siding masking needed.

quality_notes.all: Full perimeter masking around window opening on siding. Secure against wind.

tasks.name: Brush Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Stage brushes: 2-inch angular sash brush (primary workhorse for frame, sash, glass lap), 1.5-inch angular sash brush (for TDL/SDL muntin bars). Paint pots and materials. Set up access equipment per access_type: ground level, ladder, or scaffold.

quality_notes.all: Verify access equipment stability. Stage materials within reach of working position. 2-inch angular is primary; 1.5-inch for muntins.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Configure airless sprayer with 211 tip (0.011 inch orifice, 4-inch fan) for precision on small window surfaces. Install 200-mesh red filter for fine filtration. Stage 2-inch angular sash brush for back-brushing and detail work. Test spray pattern on cardboard before window application.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size. Test pattern. Stage brush for back-brushing and edge detail. 211 tip = tight 4-inch fan for window precision.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Glass masking first (most time-intensive) -> Hardware removal -> Weatherstrip protection -> Sill protection (if applicable) -> Casing protection (if applicable) -> Siding masking (spray only) -> Equipment setup last.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Window Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Cladding-specific preparation: Wood = sand 120-150 grit to remove mill glaze + fill defects + seal end-grain + tannin spot prime knots. Aluminum-clad = TSP wash + scuff-sand 180-220 grit entire surface for mechanical bonding profile. Vinyl-clad = TSP substitute clean only (no sanding). Tasks activate based on cladding_type and substrate_state.

tasks.name: Sand Wood Window Surfaces
tasks.description: Sand all wood window surfaces (frame, sash rails and stiles, muntins if TDL/SDL) with 120-150 grit to remove mill glaze, open wood grain for primer adhesion. Hand-sand only — orbital sander risks damaging glass and detailed profiles. Sand WITH the grain on all components. Pay special attention to end-grain on sash rail edges (top and bottom rails) — seal with extra primer pass.

substrate_state_rules.notes: New bare wood requires full sanding to remove mill glaze and open grain.
Factory-primed wood was sanded before priming. Light scuff only — handled by separate task.
Field-primed surface was prepped before priming.

quality_notes.QT3: Full surface sand. Even scratch pattern. No glossy mill glaze remaining.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface sand with systematic coverage. Inspect all sash edges and muntin profiles.
quality_notes.QT5: Full systematic sand. Raking light inspection. All surfaces including muntin bar edges and end-grain.

tasks.name: Scuff Sand Factory-Primed Wood Window
tasks.description: Light scuff-sand factory-primed wood window with 180-220 grit to degloss factory primer and create mechanical tooth for topcoat adhesion. Factory primer on wood is generally adequate base — this task creates adhesion profile only.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory-primed wood: light degloss/scuff before topcoat.

quality_notes.all: Light scuff only. Even degloss. No deep sanding of factory primer.

tasks.name: Fill Wood Window Defects
tasks.description: Fill nail holes, minor defects, and small damage on wood window frames and sashes with exterior-rated wood filler. Allow to cure per manufacturer spec. Sand flush with 150-220 grit. For extensive sill rot or sash rot: two-part structural epoxy (separate scope — flag for estimator).

substrate_state_rules.notes: New wood windows may have minor defects, machining marks.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill visible defects. Sand flush.
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all defects > 1/16 inch. Sand flush. Verify with raking light.
quality_notes.QT5: Fill ALL defects > 1/32 inch. Perfect flush finish. Raking light verification.

tasks.name: Tannin Knot Spot Prime (Wood)
tasks.description: Spot-apply alkyd or shellac-based stain-blocking primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_TANNIN_SPOT) to visible knots on tannin-rich wood species (cedar, redwood, Douglas fir). Brush apply to individual knots BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Prevents tannin bleed staining through finish coat. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 2.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Tannin-rich bare wood species need spot prime on knots.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot-prime visible knots. Coverage adequate.
quality_notes.QT4: Spot-prime all knots and sap streaks. Verify coverage under raking light.
quality_notes.QT5: Spot-prime all knots, sap streaks, and suspect grain areas. Shellac-based (BIN) for extreme tannin species.

tasks.notes: Conditional on wood species. Not all wood windows require tannin spot prime — pine and poplar typically do not.

tasks.name: Dust Removal After Sanding (Wood)
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from wood window surfaces with tack cloth. Required after all sanding operations before prime or finish coat application. Critical for adhesion — dust between coats causes delamination.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal. Tack cloth all surfaces. Verify no residue before coating.

tasks.name: TSP Wash Aluminum-Clad Window
tasks.description: Clean aluminum-clad window surfaces with TSP or TSP-substitute detergent to remove oxidation, chalking, dirt, and contaminants. Rinse thoroughly. Allow to dry completely before scuff-sanding. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 4.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Aluminum-clad factory finish needs cleaning before scuff-sand.

quality_notes.all: Full surface clean. Rinse thoroughly. Dry completely before sanding.

tasks.name: Scuff-Sand Aluminum-Clad Window
tasks.description: Scuff-sand entire aluminum-clad window surface with 180-220 grit to create mechanical bonding profile for corrosion-inhibiting primer. Aluminum is nonporous, slick substrate — without mechanical profile, primer will not adhere. Hand-sand all surfaces including narrow sash profiles.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Scuff-sand factory finish to create bonding profile.

quality_notes.QT3: Full surface scuff-sand. Even scratch pattern. No glossy patches.
quality_notes.QT4: Full systematic scuff-sand. Verify all surfaces including narrow profiles.
quality_notes.QT5: Full systematic scuff-sand with raking light inspection. Zero glossy spots. All narrow profiles addressed.

tasks.name: Dust Removal After Sanding (Aluminum-Clad)
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from aluminum-clad window surfaces with tack cloth. Required after scuff-sanding before corrosion-inhibiting primer application.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal. Tack cloth all surfaces. Verify no residue.

tasks.name: Clean Vinyl-Clad Window
tasks.description: Clean vinyl-clad window surfaces with TSP-substitute cleaner to remove dirt, grime, and mold. NO SANDING — vinyl surface does not benefit from abrasion and scratches compromise surface integrity. Rinse thoroughly. Allow to dry completely before bonding primer application.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Vinyl-clad factory finish needs cleaning before bonding primer.

quality_notes.all: Full surface clean. NO sanding. Rinse thoroughly. Dry completely.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Wood path: Sand prep -> Fill defects -> Dust removal -> Tannin spot prime. Aluminum path: TSP wash -> Scuff-sand -> Dust removal. Vinyl path: Clean only. Cladding_type determines which task set activates.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Window Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Cladding-driven primer paths: Wood/bare = acrylic exterior primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_ACRYLIC). Aluminum-clad = corrosion-inhibiting primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_CORROSION) — MANDATORY even over factory finish. Vinyl-clad = PVC bonding primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_BONDING_PVC) — MANDATORY even over factory finish. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips entire module. Wood with SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY skips (adequate factory base).

tasks.name: Brush Apply Acrylic Primer — Wood Window
tasks.description: Brush apply 100% acrylic exterior primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_ACRYLIC) to all bare wood window surfaces. 2-inch angular sash brush primary. Horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles (with the grain). Seal all end-grain on sash edges (top/bottom rails) with extra primer pass — critical moisture protection. 1 coat.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Bare wood requires full acrylic primer.
Wood factory primer is adequate base — skip field prime.

quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage. Seal end-grain. No holidays.
quality_notes.QT4: Full even coverage. Extra pass on end-grain. Inspect for holidays under raking light.
quality_notes.QT5: Full even coverage. Extra end-grain pass. Raking light inspection. DFT-appropriate film build.

tasks.name: Spray Apply Acrylic Primer — Wood Window
tasks.description: Spray apply 100% acrylic exterior primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_ACRYLIC) to bare wood window using 211 tip. Back-brush all sash profiles and end-grain with 2-inch angular sash brush to ensure penetration. Spray provides faster coverage on large windows; back-brushing ensures adhesion on detailed profiles.

quality_notes.QT3: Full spray coverage. Back-brush all profiles and end-grain.
quality_notes.QT4: Even spray coverage. Back-brush all profiles. Inspect for runs and sags.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision spray coverage. Back-brush all profiles. Raking light inspection.

tasks.name: Brush Apply Corrosion-Inhibiting Primer — Aluminum-Clad
tasks.description: Brush apply corrosion-inhibiting primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_CORROSION) to all aluminum-clad window surfaces. MANDATORY even over factory finish — aluminum is nonporous, requires specialized adhesion primer over scuff-sanded bonding profile. Must be applied over mechanical bonding profile (180-220 grit sanding completed in prep). 1 coat.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Aluminum-clad: field prime MANDATORY even over factory finish.

quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage over scuff-sanded surface. No holidays.
quality_notes.QT4: Full even coverage. Verify no missed areas on narrow profiles.
quality_notes.QT5: Full even coverage. Raking light inspection. All profiles addressed.

tasks.name: Spray Apply Corrosion-Inhibiting Primer — Aluminum-Clad
tasks.description: Spray apply corrosion-inhibiting primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_CORROSION) to aluminum-clad window using 211 tip. Back-brush narrow sash profiles. MANDATORY even over factory finish.

quality_notes.QT3: Full spray coverage. Back-brush profiles.
quality_notes.QT4: Even spray coverage. Back-brush all profiles. Inspect for runs.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision spray. Back-brush all profiles. Raking light inspection.

tasks.name: Brush Apply PVC Bonding Primer — Vinyl-Clad
tasks.description: Brush apply PVC bonding primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_BONDING_PVC) to all vinyl-clad window surfaces. MANDATORY — standard primers will NOT adhere to vinyl. CAUTION: bonding primer left exposed > 1 week dries like 'peanut brittle' — loses flexibility for topcoat bond. Recoat within 1 week. 1 coat.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Vinyl-clad: field prime MANDATORY even over factory finish.

quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage. Schedule topcoat within 1 week.
quality_notes.QT4: Full even coverage. Verify no holidays. Schedule topcoat within 1 week.
quality_notes.QT5: Full even coverage. Raking light inspection. Topcoat schedule coordinated for < 1 week.

tasks.name: Spray Apply PVC Bonding Primer — Vinyl-Clad
tasks.description: Spray apply PVC bonding primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_BONDING_PVC) to vinyl-clad window using 211 tip. Back-brush profiles. MANDATORY for vinyl adhesion. Recoat within 1 week.

quality_notes.QT3: Full spray coverage. Back-brush profiles. Schedule topcoat < 1 week.
quality_notes.QT4: Even spray. Back-brush all profiles. Topcoat < 1 week.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision spray. Back-brush all profiles. Raking light. Topcoat schedule coordinated.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Cladding_type + application_method determines which single prime task activates. Only one prime task runs per window. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips entire module. Wood + SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY skips. Aluminum/vinyl + SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY still requires field prime.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Window First Finish Coat
sop_modules.description: First finish coat application. Brush is PRIMARY for window painting — precision required for 1/16 inch glass lap, sash profiles, cutting in around glass. Spray only in whole-house spray context. Brush sequence: horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles (with the grain). Glass lap 1/16 inch overlap onto glass is MANDATORY — encapsulates glazing/sealant, creates weather-tight seal.

tasks.name: Brush Apply First Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush apply first finish coat to all window surfaces. 2-inch angular sash brush for frame, sash stiles and rails. 1.5-inch angular for TDL/SDL muntin bars. Brush sequence: horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles (WITH the grain). MANDATORY: maintain 1/16 inch glass lap — paint overlaps glass by exactly 1/16 inch to encapsulate glazing and create weather seal. 'Follow the sun' — paint window in shade to prevent temperature blisters.

quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage. Glass lap maintained. No runs or sags. Brush with grain.
quality_notes.QT4: Full even coverage. Consistent glass lap. No brush marks on flat profiles. Raking light check.
quality_notes.QT5: Full even coverage. Precision glass lap. Self-leveling paint for brush-mark-free finish on muntins. Raking light at multiple angles.

site_condition_rules.notes: Block all application when dew point risk is unsafe.

tasks.name: Spray Apply First Finish Coat
tasks.description: Spray apply first finish coat to window using 211 tip (4-inch tight fan). Back-brush all sash profiles, glass lap line, and muntin details with 2-inch angular sash brush. Spray provides faster coverage; back-brushing ensures even film on detailed profiles and maintains 1/16 inch glass lap. Full glass masking required for spray.

quality_notes.QT3: Full spray coverage. Back-brush all profiles and glass lap. No runs.
quality_notes.QT4: Even spray coverage. Back-brush all profiles. Verify glass lap. Inspect for sags.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision spray. Back-brush all profiles. Verify glass lap. Raking light inspection.

site_condition_rules.notes: Block spray when wind is high — overspray hazard. Block all application when dew point unsafe.

tasks.name: TDL/SDL Muntin Detail Work — First Coat
tasks.description: Detailed brush painting of individual TDL or SDL muntin bars using 1.5-inch angular sash brush. Each muntin bar face and edges must be fully coated. Glass lap maintained at each muntin-to-glass junction. TDL muntins add 1.50-2.00x production time. SDL adds 1.25x.

quality_notes.QT3: All muntin bars coated. Glass lap at each junction.
quality_notes.QT4: All muntin bars evenly coated. Consistent glass lap. No brush marks.
quality_notes.QT5: Perfect muntin coverage. Self-leveling finish. Consistent glass lap. Zero brush marks. Raking light verification.

tasks.notes: Only activates when muntin_type = TDL or SDL. GBG (grilles between glass) and none = no additional muntin work.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Finish coat task (brush or spray based on application_method) runs first. Muntin detail follows if TDL/SDL. Glass lap is maintained during both tasks.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Window Interstage Inspection & Maintenance
sop_modules.description: Between-coat inspection and maintenance. QT3: visual inspection only. QT4: light sand 220-grit + raking light inspection. QT5: hand-sand 220-320 grit + raking light at multiple angles + DFT verification. Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat

tasks.name: Intercoat Visual Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect all window surfaces between coats. Check for holidays, runs, sags, brush marks, and insufficient glass lap coverage. Mark defects for correction before next coat.

quality_notes.QT3: Visual inspection. Mark visible defects.
quality_notes.QT4: Raking light inspection. Mark all defects > 1/16 inch.
quality_notes.QT5: Raking light at multiple angles. DFT verification. Mark ALL imperfections.

tasks.name: Intercoat Sanding
tasks.description: Light sand between coats to smooth nibs, dust particles, and minor brush marks. QT4: 220-grit light scuff. QT5: 220-grit first pass then 320-grit second pass for showroom-quality smoothness. Not required at QT3.

quality_notes.QT4: Light 220-grit scuff. Smooth nibs and particles. Even coverage.
quality_notes.QT5: 220-grit first pass, 320-grit second pass. Showroom smoothness on all surfaces including muntin bars.

tasks.name: Dust Removal After Intercoat Sanding
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth after intercoat sanding. Critical before next coat application.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal. Tack cloth all surfaces.

tasks.name: Spot Repair Defects Between Coats
tasks.description: Correct defects identified during intercoat inspection. Spot-prime bare spots, fill minor surface damage, sand flush. Address runs and sags by scraping and sanding.

quality_notes.QT3: Fix visible defects. Spot-prime bare spots.
quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects. Spot-prime. Sand smooth. Raking light verify.
quality_notes.QT5: Fix ALL defects. Perfect surface. Raking light verification at multiple angles.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect -> Sand (QT4/QT5 only) -> Dust removal (QT4/QT5 only) -> Spot repair (if defects found). Full module runs after prime (if applicable) and after finish coat 1.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Window Second Finish Coat
sop_modules.description: Second (final) finish coat application. Same method as first coat. Glass lap verified on final coat. Second coat provides UV protection, color depth, and durability build. Two finish coats are standard at all quality tiers.

tasks.name: Brush Apply Second Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush apply second (final) finish coat. Same technique as first coat: horizontal rails first, vertical stiles with grain. Verify 1/16 inch glass lap coverage. Second coat builds UV resistance and color depth. 'Follow the sun' — paint in shade.

quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage. Glass lap verified. No runs or sags.
quality_notes.QT4: Full even coverage. Consistent glass lap. No brush marks. Raking light check.
quality_notes.QT5: Full even coverage. Precision glass lap. Self-leveling finish. Zero brush marks. Raking light at multiple angles.

tasks.name: Spray Apply Second Finish Coat
tasks.description: Spray apply second (final) finish coat using 211 tip. Back-brush all profiles and glass lap line. Verify glass lap coverage on final coat.

quality_notes.QT3: Full spray coverage. Back-brush profiles and glass lap.
quality_notes.QT4: Even spray. Back-brush all profiles. Verify glass lap.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision spray. Back-brush all profiles. Glass lap verified. Raking light.

tasks.name: TDL/SDL Muntin Detail Work — Second Coat
tasks.description: Detailed brush painting of individual TDL or SDL muntin bars — second (final) coat. 1.5-inch angular sash brush. Glass lap maintained at each muntin-to-glass junction. Final coat quality — zero brush marks on QT5.

quality_notes.QT3: All muntin bars coated. Glass lap maintained.
quality_notes.QT4: Even coverage. Consistent glass lap. Minimal brush marks.
quality_notes.QT5: Perfect coverage. Self-leveling finish. Zero brush marks. Precision glass lap.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Same sequence as finish coat 1. Runs after interstage module.

sop_modules.name: Double-Hung Sash Sequence (Blocking Prevention)
sop_modules.description: Double-hung specific module for preventing sash blocking (paint acts as adhesive, sealing sashes shut). Sash reversal exposes hidden rails for painting. Specific drying posture and periodic movement prevent bonding. Sliding channels, weatherstripping, and sash cords are NEVER painted — lubricate with light wax. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3.

tasks.name: Sash Reversal for Hidden Rail Access
tasks.description: Pull upper sash down, push lower sash up to expose: (1) top rail of upper sash normally hidden behind head jamb, (2) bottom rail of lower sash normally hidden behind meeting rail. These hidden surfaces must be primed and painted for moisture protection. Paint exposed rails in reversed position.

quality_notes.all: Careful sash movement to avoid damage. Free stuck sashes with window zipper if needed. Expose all hidden rails for painting.

tasks.name: Sash Drying Posture Setup
tasks.description: After painting, return sashes to nearly closed position leaving 1-inch gap at top and bottom. This prevents paint from pooling at closed joints while still allowing air circulation for drying. DO NOT close sashes fully until paint is completely cured.

quality_notes.all: 1-inch gap top and bottom. Never close fully until cured.

tasks.name: Periodic Sash Movement During Drying
tasks.description: During drying period, gently move both sashes up and down periodically (every 30-60 minutes in first 2 hours) to break any initial paint tack that could bond sash to frame. Continue until paint is past tack stage. Critical for preventing permanent sash blocking.

quality_notes.all: Gentle movement. Every 30-60 minutes in first 2 hours. Verify sashes move freely before leaving.

tasks.name: Lubricate Sliding Channels
tasks.description: Apply light wax or linseed oil to unpainted sliding channels (pulley stiles) and other sash contact points. NEVER paint these surfaces — paint in channels causes permanent sash binding. Lubrication ensures smooth sash operation after painting. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3.

quality_notes.all: Light wax in channels. Verify smooth sash operation. NEVER paint channels.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Sash reversal BEFORE painting hidden rails (integrated with finish coat workflow). Drying posture set AFTER finish coat. Periodic movement during drying. Channel lubrication AFTER final coat is touch-dry.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Window Final Inspection & Touch-Up
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough inspection of all painted window surfaces. Verify glass lap (1/16 inch), touch up defects, clean excess paint from glass beyond glass lap line using razor blade scraper. QT5: raking light at multiple angles + DFT verification.

tasks.name: Final Visual Inspection
tasks.description: Walk through all painted windows. Verify: complete coverage on all surfaces, consistent glass lap (1/16 inch overlap), no runs/sags/drips, no brush marks (QT4+), no missed areas behind hardware locations, no paint on weatherstripping or sliding channels, operable sashes move freely.

quality_notes.QT3: Visual walk-through. Verify glass lap, coverage, and sash operation.
quality_notes.QT4: Raking light inspection. Glass lap consistency. Zero visible defects from ground view.
quality_notes.QT5: Raking light at multiple angles. DFT verification on sample windows. Glass lap precision. Showroom quality.

tasks.name: Touch-Up Defects
tasks.description: Correct any defects found during final inspection. Brush touch-up on holidays, thin spots, minor drips. Blend touch-up to match surrounding finish. Use same material and brush as original application.

quality_notes.QT3: Fix visible defects. Blend to match.
quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects. Seamless blend. Raking light verify.
quality_notes.QT5: Fix ALL defects. Perfect blend. Invisible repairs. Raking light at multiple angles.

tasks.name: Glass Cleanup — Razor Scrape Excess Paint
tasks.description: Scrape excess paint from glass beyond the intentional 1/16 inch glass lap line using razor blade scraper. The 1/16 inch lap is INTENTIONAL and MUST remain — it is the weather seal. Only remove paint that extends BEYOND the lap line. Use fresh razor blades to avoid scratching glass. Wipe glass clean with damp cloth.

quality_notes.QT3: Remove obvious paint beyond lap line. Clean glass.
quality_notes.QT4: Precise scraping to lap line edge. Clean, streak-free glass.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision scraping to exact lap line. Perfect glass clarity. Zero paint beyond lap.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect -> Touch-up (if defects found) -> Glass cleanup (after touch-up is dry).

sop_modules.name: Exterior Window Protection Removal & Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Remove all masking and protection: glass masking film/tape/liquid mask removal, hardware reinstallation, weatherstrip re-insertion, sill protection teardown, casing protection removal, siding masking removal (spray). Clean and store equipment.

tasks.name: Glass Masking Removal — Tape and Film
tasks.description: Remove HDPE static-cling masking film from glass panes. Score tape at glass lap line with utility knife or razor blade before peeling for razor-sharp paint edge. Peel tape at 45-degree angle, pulling away from paint. Do NOT pull tape perpendicular — risks pulling fresh paint off frame.

quality_notes.QT3: Score and peel. Clean removal.
quality_notes.QT4: Score precisely at lap line. Peel at 45 degrees. Clean, sharp edge.
quality_notes.QT5: Precision score at exact lap line. Perfect edge definition. Zero paint pull.

tasks.name: Glass Masking Removal — Liquid Mask (TDL)
tasks.description: Score trim line at each muntin-to-glass junction and peel liquid mask from each individual glass pane. Peel in continuous sheet where possible. Use razor blade to clean any remaining residue.

quality_notes.all: Score trim line cleanly. Peel completely. Clean residue with razor.

tasks.name: Glass Masking Removal — TDL Tape and Film (Low-E)
tasks.description: Remove individual tape-and-film masking from each glass pane in TDL Low-E windows. Score tape at each muntin edge before peeling. More time-intensive than liquid mask removal due to per-pane tape.

quality_notes.all: Score at each muntin edge. Careful peel to protect Low-E coating. Clean removal.

tasks.name: Window Hardware Reinstallation
tasks.description: Reinstall all window hardware from labeled bags: locks, lifts, sash pulls, crank handles. Verify operation of each lock and mechanism. Verify sash operates smoothly with reinstalled hardware. Fixed windows: no hardware to reinstall.

quality_notes.QT3: Hardware reinstalled. Locks and lifts functional.
quality_notes.QT4: Hardware reinstalled. All mechanisms verified operational. Sash operation confirmed.
quality_notes.QT5: Hardware reinstalled with precision alignment. All mechanisms verified. Smooth sash operation confirmed.

tasks.name: Weatherstrip Reinstallation
tasks.description: Reinstall friction-fit weatherstripping that was removed during setup. Remove deep-tape from non-removable weatherstripping. Verify stripping is intact and provides proper seal. Replace any damaged stripping (flag for estimator if replacement needed).

quality_notes.all: Stripping reinstalled or tape removed. Verify seal integrity. Flag damaged stripping.

tasks.name: Sill Protection Removal
tasks.description: Remove tape and paper/film protection from exterior window sill. Verify sill surface is clean and undamaged.

quality_notes.all: Clean removal. Verify no adhesive residue on sill.

tasks.name: Casing Protection Removal
tasks.description: Remove tape from casing-to-frame junction. Verify casing finish is undamaged.

quality_notes.all: Clean removal. Verify no adhesive residue on casing.

tasks.name: Siding Masking Removal (Spray Only)
tasks.description: Remove paper and tape masking from siding adjacent to window. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

quality_notes.all: Clean removal. Verify no overspray on siding.

tasks.name: Equipment Cleaning and Storage
tasks.description: Clean all brushes, spray equipment (if used), and tools. Proper brush cleaning for reuse. Flush spray lines and clean tip/filter (if spray). Store equipment and remaining materials.

quality_notes.all: Full equipment cleaning. Brushes stored properly for reuse. Spray equipment flushed and cleaned.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Glass masking removal first (while paint is optimally cured for clean edge) -> Hardware reinstall -> Weatherstrip reinstall -> Sill/casing/siding protection removal -> Equipment clean last.

round_configurations.description: 1 prime + 2 finish coats — standard NC for bare wood and mandatory field prime on aluminum/vinyl clad
round_configurations.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD: always prime. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY: wood skips prime (use ROUND_XWIN_2FINISH), aluminum/vinyl still require field prime (use this round). Interstage runs after prime and after finish coat 1.

round_configurations.description: 2 finish coats only — factory-primed wood (adequate factory primer) or field-primed any cladding
round_configurations.notes: SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD: skip prime entirely. Also used for factory-primed wood (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY + cladding_type = wood). Interstage runs after finish coat 1 only.

round_configurations.description: Factory-primed wood — skip field prime, direct to 2 finish coats with light scuff
round_configurations.notes: Wood factory primer is adequate base for topcoat. Differs from aluminum/vinyl clad where field prime is mandatory even over factory finish. Prep module activates TSK_XWIN_SCUFF_FACTORY_WOOD for light degloss.

applicability_rules.description: MOD_XWIN_SASH_SEQUENCE only applies to double-hung windows
applicability_rules.notes: Other window types (casement, awning, fixed, bay, bow) do not have sliding sash blocking risk.

applicability_rules.description: Liquid mask tasks only activate when Low-E = false AND muntin_type = TDL
applicability_rules.notes: HARD STOP: liquid mask PROHIBITED on Low-E glass.

applicability_rules.description: Spray equipment and siding masking tasks only activate for spray application
applicability_rules.notes: Brush is PRIMARY for windows. Spray only in whole-house spray context.

applicability_rules.description: Muntin detail tasks only activate for TDL and SDL windows
applicability_rules.notes: GBG (grilles between glass) and none = no additional muntin work.
Field-primed surfaces go direct to finish coats.

applicability_rules.description: Wood factory-primed windows skip field prime (but aluminum/vinyl do not)
applicability_rules.notes: Per COMPAT-XWIN-007: factory-primed wood may skip field prime. Factory-primed aluminum/vinyl STILL require field prime.

applicability_rules.description: Hardware tasks skip for fixed windows (no operable hardware)
applicability_rules.notes: Fixed windows have no operable hardware to remove/reinstall.

applicability_rules.description: Weatherstrip tasks skip for fixed windows (no weatherstripping)

exclusions.reason: Belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING). This spec covers the window unit itself: frame, sash, muntin bars.
Interior jamb, stool interior face, interior casing belong to SF_WINDOW_INT_NC_v1. Scope boundary at window frame-to-jamb junction.

exclusions.scope: Glass masking for whole-house siding spray
exclusions.reason: When spraying SIDING (not window), the siding/trim spec owns glass protection. This spec only masks glass when painting the WINDOW itself.
Extensive decay requiring two-part structural epoxy or wood Dutchman repairs is separate scope. Flag for estimator.

Traditional glazing compound replacement is a separate conditional scope. Addressed in research.json but not included as a standard SOP module for NC windows (new construction typically has modern glazing).

assumptions.value: Three masking paths: (1) tape+film for Low-E and standard single-lite/SDL/GBG, (2) liquid mask for non-Low-E TDL, (3) tape+film per-pane for Low-E TDL
assumptions.note: Doctrine explicit on Low-E prohibition for liquid mask and masking method selection.

assumptions.value: Sash blocking prevention module only applies to double-hung window type
assumptions.note: Doctrine section 3 specifically addresses double-hung sash blocking. Other window types have different hinge/operation mechanisms not susceptible to blocking.

assumptions.value: Brush is PRIMARY application method for windows; spray is conditional on whole-house spray context
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms brush is primary for window precision work. Spray tasks included for whole-house spray context.

assumptions.value: Factory-primed wood windows may skip field prime; factory-primed aluminum/vinyl MUST receive field prime
assumptions.source: resolution.json substrate_state notes; materials.json compatibility rules
assumptions.note: Resolution explicitly differentiates: wood factory primer is adequate, aluminum/vinyl factory finish requires specialized adhesion primer.

assumptions.value: Intercoat sanding is QT4/QT5 only; QT3 gets visual inspection only
assumptions.note: Resolution explicit: QT3 = visual inspect, QT4 = 220-grit + raking light, QT5 = 220-320 grit + raking light + DFT.

task_summary.notes: 51 total tasks across 9 modules. 28 binary (protection, equipment, hardware, masking removal, sash sequence, standard operations), 21 qt_scaled (prep sanding, fill, prime, finish, inspection, touch-up — rate varies by quality tier), 2 qt_conditional (intercoat sanding and dust removal — QT4/QT5 only). Task count reflects 3 cladding paths x 2 application methods for prime tasks (6 prime variants), 3 masking method variants for setup and teardown.
